chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Synthesis exemplar — Sample 1A, score 1-4-0 (5/6)
chunks.content: Synthesis essay (GPS / mapping-software prompt) scored 5/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 4, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible position in paragraph 1 — 'GPS is an extremely useful tool that presents no negative aspects in the world of driving.' Evidence & Commentary (4): specific evidence supports all claims in a line of reasoning that GPS makes travel easier, e.g. Source D ('induces a state of rest' so drivers 'drive safer'); commentary consistently explains how the evidence supports the reasoning ('making it far easier for others'). Sophistication (0): not demonstrated.

chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Synthesis exemplar — Sample 1B, score 1-3-0 (4/6)
chunks.content: Synthesis essay scored 4/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 3, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible position that GPS 'has had many negative effects on residential areas and the way that motorists understand navigation.' Evidence & Commentary (3): specific evidence supports all claims (Source A police chief, '250,000 wazers'); commentary explains how some evidence supports the line of reasoning, but some commentary (paragraph 4) does not clearly connect the evidence to the claim, so it falls short of 4. Sophistication (0): not demonstrated.

chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Synthesis exemplar — Sample 1C, score 1-2-0 (3/6)
chunks.content: Synthesis essay scored 3/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 2, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible position about difficulties using GPS. Evidence & Commentary (2): relevant evidence from three sources, some specific (Foderaro quote), but commentary explains only how some evidence relates to the argument and does not explain connections/progression between claims, so no clear line of reasoning is established. Sophistication (0): not demonstrated.
